payload.feature:
Decision 0035 is accepted (ruled 2026-09-03; docs/decisions/0035-effort-is-part-of-the-hire.md). Enact it. Read the decision first: each of its seven rulings names an enforcement binding, and those bindings are this commission — nothing beyond them.

What to build:

1. contracts/seat-record.v2.schema.json beside v1, and v1 is never edited (ruling 7). v2 adds `effort` to the per-turn checkpoint, the finishing checkpoint and the successful result, described as configuration, never as a report; and `reasoning_output_tokens`, a reported subset of `output_tokens` the way `cache_read_tokens` is a subset of `input_tokens`, never added to a total a second time, absent where a harness reports no per-turn figure — never zero, never back-filled from the run total. Records validate against the version their run's engine wrote (brokkr-store validator). Add the v2 row to contracts/README.md and pin v2 in crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/frozen_contracts.rs beside v1.

2. The built-in folds in brokkr-protocol::adapters and their conformance shims (ruling 3, ruling 4). codex: `effort` per turn from the thread record's turn_context.effort through the decision 0032 locator; `reasoning_output_tokens` per turn from turn.completed.usage; and map the `cache_write_input_tokens` it already receives onto the `cache_write_tokens` v1 defines. claude: `effort` from the harness's own echo beside each assistant record; reasoning only in its result (output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens), so per-turn stays absent. dsh: `effort` is the 0031 sentinel `not reported` — the lanes carry a real control but nothing echoes it. exec: `not applicable`. Driver conformance covers every built-in driver.

3. Every model pin carries an effort pin (ruling 5). Where decision 0031 ruling 2 requires a concrete model, an effort-bearing driver (claude, codex, dsh) also requires a concrete effort, in the vocabulary that driver's adapter declares; exec needs none. In the agent library each `models` candidate gains a companion effort, so a charter names the effort it hires as it names the model. Bundle compilation scans the fully composed seat tree and reports every unpinned seat, member and step in one refusal beside the existing model refusal, with the repair; `brokkr doctor --bundle` exposes the same refusal. Then pin an effort in every shipped agent, bundle and recipe so that all of bundles/self, bundles/verify and recipes/* compile: their digests move, and that is the identity change ruling 5 intends — re-pin the witnesses in crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/witness_digests.rs and crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/compose_tests.rs, and say why in the commit. Choose each effort as the plainest reading of what the seat does today (the driver's default where a default exists); do not tune.

4. brokkr-view derives the pin and the applied effort as separate cells, both labelled configuration, and old-journal absence stays absent with no fallback (ruling 6). Reasoning sums exactly as documented: extend docs/guides/driver-authoring.md with the sum rules, the v2 fields, and the sentence ruling 2 asks for — `model` is the provider's claim, not proof — and mirror that wording in every readout that labels the field (brokkr costs, brokkr inspect, the tui).

Do not touch: the wire protocol (forge-driver/v1 — effort and reasoning are additive payload facts, like model before them), any journal row, any frozen evaluator fixture, seat-record v1, or the dsh headless profile (its thin record is a finding the decision deliberately leaves unruled). Full gate as the verify seat knows it, exact coverage included; every new refusal has a test that trips it.

result.notes: Framed decision 0035's enactment: seat-record v2 beside the frozen v1 (effort + reasoning_output_tokens), the codex/claude/dsh/exec folds and conformance, an effort-pin compile refusal beside the model-pin one plus repin of every shipped agent/bundle/recipe and the two witness-digest test files, and the brokkr-view/doctor/driver-authoring.md readout updates. Task file names concrete files (adapters.rs fold functions, bundle.rs enforce_model_pins/enforce_model_policy, seat_record.rs validator, witness_digests.rs WITNESSES array) and the coherent-but-open design question (how a record's target schema version is known at validation time). Request is coherent and does not violate any frozen contract as framed.
